review_evidence: README identifies the project as a Lean 4 port of s2n-bignum formal verification, including big-integer definitions, ARM state/instruction semantics, specification framework and machine-checked correctness proofs.
A complete scan of 23 Lean files found 64 theorem/lemma/example declarations and 214 declaration-style items.

Bignum/Arm/Spec.lean defines eventually, ensures, ARM transition/program predicates and frame conditions and proves eventually_mono, ensures_trans, eventually_exec, ensures_of_exec and maychange lemmas, providing reusable verification semantics rather than mere bindings.
summary: Reviewed bignum and retain its Lean port of verified cryptographic arithmetic and machine semantics.

review_evidence: Declaration grep over all 46 files: 35 files have one or more declarations; the largest, BignumTest/Arm/State.lean (33877 bytes), has 609 declaration lines, 607 of them example/theorem.

11 files have zero declarations and are import aggregators: Bignum.lean, Bignum/Arm.lean, Bignum/ArmOld.lean, Bignum/ArmOld/Common.lean, Bignum/ArmOld/Common/Basic.lean, Bignum/ArmOld/Machine.lean, Bignum/ArmOld/Tutorial.lean, Bignum/BitVec.lean, Bignum/Component.lean, Bignum/Memory.lean, Bignum/Relational.lean; I read each completely (copyright header, `module`, `public import` lines). They stay primary-eligible per FILTER-007/FD-016.

BignumTest/ArmOld/Machine/Decode.lean and BignumTest/ArmOld/Machine/Loader.lean have zero declarations; I read both completely: `public meta import`, `open Bignum.ArmOld`, and #eval checks of extractBits, compareBytes, formatBytesAsLeanDef and hexDump with expected results. These are executable formal commands that name library identifiers, so they stay retained under FILTER-002.
BignumTest/Memory.lean and BignumTest/Arm/ShiftType.lean read completely: rfl-proved example statements about ByteList.ofNatLE/ofIntLE and ShiftType.LSL/LSR/ASR/ROR.shift.
Bignum/Arm/InstructionLemmas.lean opening read: theorems XZR_zero, WZR_zero, zero_register, shifted_LSL_zero about ARM register components.
Bignum/ArmOld/Tutorial/Simple.lean opening read: port of s2n-bignum/arm/tutorial/simple.ml, a proof about a two-instruction ARM program.
grep for transcript markers (User:/Assistant:/```) matched 11 files; the matches are code fences inside Lean doc comments, not transcript dumps.
summary: Surveyed all 46 listed Lean files under Bignum/, BignumTest/ and Bignum.lean with a per-file grep count of declaration keywords (def/theorem/lemma/structure/inductive/abbrev/instance/class/example/axiom/macro/syntax) and theorem/lemma/example counts. Read completely the 11 import aggregators, BignumTest/Memory.lean, BignumTest/Arm/ShiftType.lean, BignumTest/ArmOld/Machine/Decode.lean and BignumTest/ArmOld/Machine/Loader.lean, and read the opening sections of BignumTest/Arm/State.lean, Bignum/Arm/InstructionLemmas.lean and Bignum/ArmOld/Tutorial/Simple.lean. The library files hold ARM machine semantics, bit-vector and memory definitions, and lemmas about them; the test files hold rfl-checked example statements or #eval checks of the decoder and ELF loader. The import aggregators are module-level Lean files with `module` and `public import` commands; FILTER-007 keeps them primary-eligible under FD-016 ranking. No file is established as free of formal content that search needs, so every file is retained.
